bundles.title: LLM memory architecture
bundles.central_question: How does an LLM memory architecture separate retrieval from canonical updates?
bundles.summary: Retrieval supplies selected owner context while a reviewed pending draft proposes any canonical update.

structured_content.definition: An LLM memory architecture retrieves explicitly selected owner knowledge as reference data, then submits a complete proposed final card as a private pending draft. Only the owner can approve, merge, or update canonical knowledge.
key_points: Retrieval does not mutate canonical knowledge.
A merge proposal contains the complete proposed final card, not a partial patch.

resolution_proposal.reason: The selected conversation adds a review boundary to the same existing concept.
